faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Straight answers to the questions investors ask us most.

items.q: Can foreigners buy property in Dubai?
items.a: Yes. Foreign nationals can buy freehold property, with full ownership, in Dubai’s designated freehold areas. Ownership is registered with the Dubai Land Department, and you receive a title deed in your name.

items.q: Can I buy without travelling to Dubai?
items.a: Yes. We run video viewings, send verified documents and arrange digital reservations. Signing can be completed remotely or through a power of attorney. Your advisor coordinates each step through to the title deed.

Off-plan payments go into regulated escrow accounts and are released to the developer as construction progresses. Every project must be registered, and every advert must carry a DLD permit. Delays can still happen, so we show each developer’s delivery record before you commit.

items.q: What does it cost to buy?
items.a: The main cost is the Dubai Land Department transfer fee of 4% of the price, plus registration and administration fees. Resale purchases usually also involve an agency fee, and mortgages add registration and bank fees. Your advisor gives you an exact breakdown for any property.

items.q: How does the Golden Visa work?
items.a: Investing AED 2M or more in Dubai property may qualify you for a renewable 10-year residency visa, which can include your family. Conditions apply to off-plan and mortgaged properties, and we check your eligibility for free.

items.q: Are there taxes on property income?
items.a: The UAE does not charge personal income tax on rental income or capital gains tax for individuals. You may still owe tax in your home country, so speak to a tax adviser there.
Yes. Many UAE banks lend to non-residents, typically up to 50–60% of the property value, subject to income and credit checks. We introduce you to trusted mortgage partners.

items.q: What rental yield can I expect?
items.a: Typical gross yields in Dubai range from about 6% to 8%, depending on area, property type and how it’s let. Every Buildcaps listing shows an estimate based on Dubai Land Department data.

Off-plan projects are paid in stages. For example, a 20/55/25 plan means 20% on booking, 55% during construction and 25% on handover. Some developers offer post-handover plans that spread payments over several years after you receive the keys.
Usually, yes. Most developers allow you to resell (assign) an off-plan unit once a set percentage of the price has been paid. The rules differ by developer, and we confirm them before you buy.

items.q: How do I verify a listing is genuine?
items.a: Every legitimate Dubai property advert carries a Trakheesi permit number and QR code issued by the Dubai Land Department. Scan it to confirm the listing and the broker. Every Buildcaps listing shows its permit.

items.q: Who manages my property after I buy?
items.a: We can find tenants, collect rent and handle maintenance through our property management service, or set you up with a trusted short-term rental operator.

sections.body: Service providers that help us run the website and appointments (hosting, email, calendar), and developers or banks when you ask us to involve them.

sections.title: How long we keep it
sections.body: As long as we need it to serve you and to meet legal obligations. After that we delete or anonymise it.

sections.title: Your rights
sections.body: You can ask to access, correct, delete or transfer your data, withdraw consent, or object to processing, by emailing us.

sections.title: International transfers
sections.body: Some providers process data outside the UAE. We only use providers that offer appropriate safeguards.

cookies.title: Cookie policy
cookies.summary: How the Buildcaps website uses cookies and how to manage them.

sections.title: What cookies are
sections.body: Small files your browser stores so a website works properly and remembers your choices.

sections.title: Essential cookies
sections.body: Needed to run the site, for example to remember your language. They are always on.

sections.title: Your preferences
sections.body: Your display currency and area unit are stored in your browser so the site remembers them.

sections.title: Analytics cookies
sections.body: With your consent, we measure visits and conversions to improve the site. You can change your choice at any time.

sections.title: Managing cookies
sections.body: You can also block or delete cookies in your browser settings. Some features may stop working.
